import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    # Products and machines and periods
    "products": [0, 1],
    "machines": [0, 1],
    "periods": [0, 1, 2],

    # Costs
    "setup_cost": 149.1695690337089,
    "startup_cost": 69.24269269143792,
    "holding_cost": {0: 1.080318154052025, 1: 1.143069947055348},
    "backlog_cost": {0: 6.798895023015501, 1: 6.372651501311341},

    # Demands: demand[product][period]
    "demand": {
        0: {0: 22.92965094851524, 1: 19.03396834281949, 2: 18.90167422155575},
        1: {0: 19.80185049682801, 1: 24.22810173621122, 2: 16.84556169689551},
    },

    # Machine capacities
    "capacity": {0: 76.7045484622153, 1: 69.3695364951939},

    # Startup time charged per product-machine-period startup
    "startup_time": 1.0,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=d["products"])
    model.M = pyo.Set(initialize=d["machines"])
    model.T = pyo.Set(initialize=d["periods"])

    # x[m,p,t]: production quantity of product p on machine m in period t
    # "determining the exact quantity of each product to produce on each machine in each period"
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.M, model.P, model.T,
                      within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # y[m,p,t]: binary, whether product p is produced on machine m in period t
    # "determining whether to produce each product on each machine in each period"
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.M, model.P, model.T,
                      within=pyo.Binary)

    # z[m,p,t]: binary, whether a machine startup occurs for product p on machine m in period t
    # "deciding whether to start up each machine for each product in each period"
    model.z = pyo.Var(model.M, model.P, model.T,
                      within=pyo.Binary)

    # I[p,t]: inventory of product p carried over after period t
    # "deciding how much inventory to carry over"
    model.I = pyo.Var(model.P, model.T,
                      within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # B[p,t]: backlog of product p after period t
    # "or how much demand to backlog for each product in each period"
    model.B = pyo.Var(model.P, model.T,
                      within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Objective: minimize total operational costs
    # "Minimize the total operational costs, which include production setup costs,
    #  machine startup costs, inventory holding costs, and backlogging costs"
    def obj_rule(m):
        setup = sum(d["setup_cost"] * m.y[mm, pp, tt]
                    for mm in m.M for pp in m.P for tt in m.T)
        startup = sum(d["startup_cost"] * m.z[mm, pp, tt]
                      for mm in m.M for pp in m.P for tt in m.T)
        holding = sum(d["holding_cost"][pp] * m.I[pp, tt]
                      for pp in m.P for tt in m.T)
        backlog = sum(d["backlog_cost"][pp] * m.B[pp, tt]
                      for pp in m.P for tt in m.T)
        return setup + startup + holding + backlog

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Setup linking: x[m,p,t] <= capacity[m] * y[m,p,t]
    # "determining the exact quantity of each product to produce on each machine in each period"
    # "production and startup decisions must be binary"
    def setup_link_rule(m, mm, pp, tt):
        return m.x[mm, pp, tt] <= d["capacity"][mm] * m.y[mm, pp, tt]

    model.setup_link = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.P, model.T,
                                      rule=setup_link_rule)

    # Capacity: production quantity plus startup time cannot exceed machine capacity
    # "The production quantity on each machine, plus the startup time, cannot exceed the machine's capacity"
    def capacity_rule(m, mm, tt):
        return (sum(m.x[mm, pp, tt] for pp in m.P)
                + d["startup_time"] * sum(m.z[mm, pp, tt] for pp in m.P)
                <= d["capacity"][mm])

    model.capacity = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.T, rule=capacity_rule)

    # One product per machine per period
    # "Each machine can only produce one product at a time in any given period"
    def one_product_rule(m, mm, tt):
        return sum(m.y[mm, pp, tt] for pp in m.P) <= 1

    model.one_product = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.T, rule=one_product_rule)

    # Startup logic for period 0: z[m,p,0] >= y[m,p,0]
    # "If a machine is used for production in a period but was not used in the previous period,
    #  a startup cost is incurred"
    # assumption: first-period use counts as a startup
    def startup_first_rule(m, mm, pp):
        return m.z[mm, pp, 0] >= m.y[mm, pp, 0]

    model.startup_first = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.P,
                                         rule=startup_first_rule)

    # Startup logic for t >= 1: z[m,p,t] >= y[m,p,t] - y[m,p,t-1]
    # "If a machine is used for production in a period but was not used in the previous period,
    #  a startup cost is incurred"
    # assumption: only z >= y[t] - y[t-1] (z may be 1 even without a real startup)
    def startup_rule(m, mm, pp, tt):
        if tt == 0:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        return m.z[mm, pp, tt] >= m.y[mm, pp, tt] - m.y[mm, pp, tt - 1]

    model.startup = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.P, model.T,
                                   rule=startup_rule)

    # Inventory balance: prod + I[t-1] + B[t] == demand + I[t] + B[t-1]
    # "total production of each product across all machines, plus any inventory carried over
    #  from the previous period, minus any backlog from the previous period, equals the demand
    #  for that product in the current period, plus any inventory carried forward, minus any
    #  backlogged demand"
    # assumption: inventory_balance_orientation = prod + I[t-1] + B[t] == demand + I[t] + B[t-1]
    def balance_rule(m, pp, tt):
        production = sum(m.x[mm, pp, tt] for mm in m.M)
        inv_prev = m.I[pp, tt - 1] if tt > 0 else 0
        backlog_prev = m.B[pp, tt - 1] if tt > 0 else 0
        return (production + inv_prev + m.B[pp, tt]
                == d["demand"][pp][tt] + m.I[pp, tt] + backlog_prev)

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.P, model.T, rule=balance_rule)

    return model

import pyomo.environ as pyo

# All numeric constants from the problem statement.
DATA = {
    "products": [0, 1],
    "machines": [0, 1],
    "periods": [0, 1, 2],
    # Costs
    "setup_cost": 149.1695690337089,          # production setup cost per run
    "startup_cost": 69.24269269143792,        # machine startup cost
    "holding_cost": {0: 1.080318154052025, 1: 1.143069947055348},
    "backlog_cost": {0: 6.798895023015501, 1: 6.372651501311341},
    # Demands: demand[p][t]
    "demand": {
        0: {0: 22.92965094851524, 1: 19.03396834281949, 2: 18.90167422155575},
        1: {0: 19.80185049682801, 1: 24.22810173621122, 2: 16.84556169689551},
    },
    # Machine capacity
    "capacity": {0: 76.7045484622153, 1: 69.3695364951939},
    # Startup time charged per product-machine-period startup
    "startup_time": 1.0,  # assumption: startup_time = 1.0 per the modelling decisions
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=d["products"])
    model.M = pyo.Set(initialize=d["machines"])
    model.T = pyo.Set(initialize=d["periods"])

    # Production quantity of product p on machine m in period t
    # "determining the exact quantity of each product to produce on each machine in each period"
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.M, model.P, model.T,
                      within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Production setup indicator: 1 if product p is produced on machine m in period t
    # "determining whether to produce each product on each machine in each period"
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.M, model.P, model.T,
                      within=pyo.Binary)

    # Machine startup indicator: 1 if a startup occurs for product p on machine m in period t
    # "deciding whether to start up each machine for each product in each period"
    model.z = pyo.Var(model.M, model.P, model.T,
                      within=pyo.Binary)

    # Inventory carried over for product p at end of period t
    # "deciding how much inventory to carry over ... for each product in each period"
    model.I = pyo.Var(model.P, model.T,
                      within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Backlog for product p at end of period t
    # "or how much demand to backlog for each product in each period"
    model.B = pyo.Var(model.P, model.T,
                      within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Objective: minimize total operational costs
    # "Minimize the total operational costs, which include production setup costs,
    #  machine startup costs, inventory holding costs, and backlogging costs"
    def obj_rule(m):
        setup = sum(d["setup_cost"] * m.y[mm, pp, tt]
                    for mm in m.M for pp in m.P for tt in m.T)
        startup = sum(d["startup_cost"] * m.z[mm, pp, tt]
                      for mm in m.M for pp in m.P for tt in m.T)
        holding = sum(d["holding_cost"][pp] * m.I[pp, tt]
                      for pp in m.P for tt in m.T)
        backlog = sum(d["backlog_cost"][pp] * m.B[pp, tt]
                      for pp in m.P for tt in m.T)
        return setup + startup + holding + backlog

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Setup linking: x[m,p,t] <= capacity[m] * y[m,p,t]
    # assumption: setup_linking_big_m = capacity[m]
    def setup_link_rule(m, mm, pp, tt):
        return m.x[mm, pp, tt] <= d["capacity"][mm] * m.y[mm, pp, tt]

    model.setup_link = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.P, model.T,
                                      rule=setup_link_rule)

    # Machine capacity: production quantity plus startup time <= capacity
    # "The production quantity on each machine, plus the startup time,
    #  cannot exceed the machine's capacity"
    def capacity_rule(m, mm, tt):
        return (sum(m.x[mm, pp, tt] for pp in m.P)
                + d["startup_time"] * sum(m.z[mm, pp, tt] for pp in m.P)
                <= d["capacity"][mm])

    model.capacity = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.T, rule=capacity_rule)

    # Each machine can only produce one product at a time in any given period
    # "Each machine can only produce one product at a time in any given period"
    def one_product_rule(m, mm, tt):
        return sum(m.y[mm, pp, tt] for pp in m.P) <= 1

    model.one_product = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.T, rule=one_product_rule)

    # Startup logic for period 0: z[m,p,0] >= y[m,p,0]
    # assumption: startup_logic_period_zero
    def startup_first_rule(m, mm, pp):
        return m.z[mm, pp, 0] >= m.y[mm, pp, 0]

    model.startup_first = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.P,
                                         rule=startup_first_rule)

    # Startup logic for t >= 1: z[m,p,t] >= y[m,p,t] - y[m,p,t-1]
    # "If a machine is used for production in a period but was not used in the
    #  previous period, a startup cost is incurred"
    # assumption: startup_indicator_upper_bound (only z >= y[t] - y[t-1])
    def startup_rule(m, mm, pp, tt):
        if tt == 0:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        return m.z[mm, pp, tt] >= m.y[mm, pp, tt] - m.y[mm, pp, tt - 1]

    model.startup = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.P, model.T, rule=startup_rule)

    # Inventory balance:
    # I[t-1] + prod - B[t-1] == demand + I[t] - B[t]
    # "total production of each product across all machines, plus any inventory
    #  carried over from the previous period, minus any backlog from the previous
    #  period, equals the demand for that product in the current period, plus any
    #  inventory carried forward, minus any backlogged demand"
    # assumption: inventory_balance_orientation
    def balance_rule(m, pp, tt):
        prod = sum(m.x[mm, pp, tt] for mm in m.M)
        if tt == 0:
            prev_I = 0
            prev_B = 0
        else:
            prev_I = m.I[pp, tt - 1]
            prev_B = m.B[pp, tt - 1]
        return (prev_I + prod - prev_B
                == d["demand"][pp][tt] + m.I[pp, tt] - m.B[pp, tt])

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.P, model.T, rule=balance_rule)

    # Demand satisfaction: cumulative production >= cumulative demand
    # "while meeting customer demand for each product in each period"
    # assumption: demand_satisfaction_constraint
    def demand_sat_rule(m, pp, tt):
        return (sum(m.x[mm, pp, t2] for mm in m.M for t2 in m.T if t2 <= tt)
                >= sum(d["demand"][pp][t2] for t2 in m.T if t2 <= tt))

    model.demand_sat = pyo.Constraint(model.P, model.T, rule=demand_sat_rule)

    return model
